- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- In absence of strong sentiment, model often underestimates mean-reversion trend; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with historical mean.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.22) and price is rising, model underestimates upside; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–5 days; shift forecast 1–3 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out; use median of recent 5-day trend instead of 30-day mean for correction.
